validity.researcher_notes: Existence and identity corroborated by 5 distinct-outlet sources spanning 1998-2021, at least 3 independent origins: JPDO's own corporate history (jpdo.co.jp/ehistory.html, Wayback 2018 capture -- JPDO founded 1998 specifically to pursue this project, name formalized 2007); Reuters 2014-10-15, which itself explicitly relays the Nikkei newspaper's original scoop ('the Nikkei reported, citing diplomatic sources it did not identify') but adds independent value -- a Japanese METI official's on-record denial that Tokyo had received any such offer (so NOT counted as independent of Nikkei's underlying report, but corroborates that a proposal-related event occurred around Oct 2014); caspianbarrel.org 2014-11-11, a distinct origin carrying a direct on-record Miller quote ('Japan has submitted the proposal to build the gas pipeline to Hokkaido and, possibly, Tokyo... We have not responded yet') plus a TASS-sourced quote from Russian Energy Minister Novak calling the project 'economically groundless' -- independent of both Reuters and Nikkei; Nikkei Asia's own later 2017-08 piece ('Japan-Russia gas pipeline mostly a pipe dream,' detailed technical/route reporting, 1,500km, $6bn, Sakhalin-Hokkaido-Tohoku-Kanto routing); and Vedomosti 2021-05-20 (Gazprom deputy chair Elena Burmistrova's on-the-record statement that the Japan pipeline is 'not being considered' -- the cancellation source, itself corroborating Miller's 2016 and Medvedev's 2017 on-record remarks quoted in the same article). No indication this row duplicates or should be merged with any other GEM Russia-gas entry; it is the unique Sakhalin-Japan cross-border concept in this batch.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Annual-update status review: Status='cancelled' (CancelledYear=2021) remains correct as recorded. The underlying evidence is Vedomosti's 2021-05-20 direct quote from Gazprom deputy chairwoman Elena Burmistrova stating the Japan pipeline 'is not being considered.' Searched specifically for 2022-2026 revival signals -- Russia-Japan energy relations deteriorated sharply after February 2022 (sanctions, Japan joining the G7 sanctions regime against Russia, Sakhalin-2 LNG ownership disputes), which if anything reinforces rather than undermines the 2021 cancellation; no source of any kind (Russian, Japanese, or English-language trade press) from 2022-2026 was found proposing revival, renewed talks, or any change to the project's cancelled status. Verdict: confirm, no change. ShelvedCancelledType should remain 'confirmed' (an explicit official statement, not an inference) -- matches BRIEF.md's own expectation for this row.
